core_obligations: The sheaf condition (proof lines 6285-6300): for a covering of an object the author describes the restriction of a pair consisting of a section and a morphism into the localizing object, and observes that a compatible family forces the corresponding morphisms to become equal on the pairwise products.

Gluing (proof lines 6301-6307): the hypothesis that the topology is weaker than the canonical one gives a unique morphism into the localizing object gluing the given ones, and the sheaf condition for the given sheaf glues the sections, which establishes the sheaf condition for the describing presheaf.
proof_roadmap: Check the sheaf condition for the presheaf describing the lower shriek.
Use the subcanonicality to glue the morphisms into the localizing object.
Use the sheaf condition of the given sheaf to glue the sections.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that over a site with subcanonical topology the lower shriek along a localization is computed without sheafification, by the coproduct displayed, so that the description of the companion lemma needs no sheafification (statement lines 6267-6282). The proof is a complete verification of the sheaf condition for the describing presheaf: the restrictions of a compatible family are described and shown to force equality of the morphisms on the pairwise products (proof lines 6285-6300); subcanonicality then provides a unique morphism gluing them and the sheaf condition for the given sheaf glues the sections (proof lines 6301-6307), which is exactly what is needed. The non-formal content is the verification of the sheaf condition. The claim is H2: a written-out verification with each input named.
